newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end at record high after bumpy day.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end at record high after bumpy day.

text.p: Swedish shares prices ended at a record high on Thursday after a bumpy session.
The bourse's general index closed at 2,557.11, up 0.13 percent, in turnover of 4.2 billion crowns.
A late recovery in drug company Astra, sparked by gains by U.S. counterparts, boosted market indicies. The share closed up 1.5 crowns at 344.5.
Telecoms group Ericsson, the session's most traded share, fell 4.5 crowns to 241.5 on U.S. sector trends.
Insurance company Trygg-Hansa closed flat at 156 crowns after having jumped more than eight percent in the session.
The company posted a 31 percent rise in 1996 profits and unveiled plans to buy back two billion crowns worth of shares which was welcomed by the market.

Roller bearing maker SKF rose over four percent to 172 crowns after posting a 1996 profit after financial items of 2.41 billion crowns. A Reuter poll found profit expectations ranged between 2.22 billion and 2.69 billion crowns.
Forestry shares continued to gain, with the sector index rising 1.44 percent, helped by the stronger dollar.
